terms.comment: Livy’s id diēī iter est with an hour for the day. We have found no classical instance with hōrae.

phrases.latin: Quot hōrārum iter est? — Sēmihōrae; mox aderimus.
phrases.english: How long does it take? — Half an hour; we’ll soon be there.

phrases.latin: quō cum Perseus obviam Amphipolī omnī solūtus custōdiā prōcessisset — id diēī iter est —
phrases.english: when Perseus, freed from all guard, had come out to meet him at Amphipolis (it is a day’s journey)

sources: Lewis & Short: hora · Lewis & Short: dies · Lewis & Short: iter
